title: Permanent Lighting Systems App Control Ranked (2026)
body_markdown:
Permanent lighting systems stopped being a novelty around 2020 and turned into a real product category by 2026, and the software behind them now matters as much as the LED chip inside the channel. This guide ranks the systems homeowners in South Jersey, Eastern Pennsylvania, and Northern Delaware ask about most, based on how their apps actually handle zone control, scheduling, and smart home integration.


**TL;DR**

- Gemstone Lights wins for full-color scene design and Alexa/Google integration in 2026.
- Trex Lighting (DEKOR) is the best permanent lighting systems app control features pick for homes built around outdoor living spaces.
- EverLights is the simplest app for homeowners who want zone control without a learning curve.
- Kichler Permanent Lighting pairs roofline and path lighting in one app for full-property control.
- Lumilum favors installer-programmed scenes over a consumer-facing app, which suits hands-off homeowners.


## Why this matters

A permanent lighting system is only as good as the app that runs it. Buy the wrong platform and you end up with a beautiful LED install that drops its Wi-Fi connection every time it rains, or a scheduling menu so clunky you stop changing colors after the first month.

The roofline is also where your gutters live, and any crew installing [permanent lighting cost breakdown](https://cleangutterslighting.com/blog/how-much-do-permanent-christmas-lights-cost-in) options should be checking channel condition and fascia integrity at the same time. That overlap is why installers who work gutters and lighting together, like CleanGutters Lighting, end up giving more useful advice on system choice than a lighting-only sales rep would.

## What makes the best permanent lighting systems app control features

- **Zone control granularity** — can you address individual roof sections independently, or is it all-or-nothing
- **Scheduling and astronomical timers** — does the app trigger lighting off sunset/sunrise automatically or require manual resets
- **Color and scene customization** — RGBW range, saved presets, holiday-to-everyday switching
- **Smart home integration** — Alexa, Google Home, or Apple Home compatibility
- **Connectivity reliability** — 2.4GHz Wi-Fi versus Bluetooth mesh, and how the system behaves during outages
- **Installer support model** — whether the homeowner programs scenes themselves or the installer sets them at commissioning

### At a glance

| System | Best for | Standout app feature | Key limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemstone Lights | Full-color scene design | Custom scene builder with smart home links | Requires steady 2.4GHz Wi-Fi at the roofline |
| Trex Lighting (DEKOR) | Outdoor living spaces | Unified control with deck/hardscape lighting | Less depth on holiday-specific presets |
| EverLights | Simple zone control | Streamlined app, minimal setup steps | Fewer advanced scene options |
| Kichler Permanent Lighting | Whole-property integration | Roofline and landscape path lights in one app | Menu structure less intuitive for scene layering |
| Lumilum | Installer-programmed scenes | Professional commissioning, low homeowner overhead | Homeowner has less day-to-day app control |

## 1. Gemstone Lights: best permanent lighting for full-color scene design

Gemstone Lights builds its reputation on the app, not just the fixture. The platform lets you build custom color scenes zone by zone and save them for instant recall, which matters if you switch from a neutral warm-white look on Tuesday to a full-color display for a weekend event.

**Gemstone Lights pros:**
- Deep scene customization across individual roofline zones
- Alexa and Google Home integration for voice control
- Astronomical timer handles sunset/sunrise automatically, no manual resets

**Gemstone Lights cons:**
- Performance depends on a strong 2.4GHz Wi-Fi signal reaching the roofline, which older homes sometimes lack without a signal booster
- More menu depth means a longer initial setup for homeowners who just want "on at dusk, off at 11"

**Best for:** homeowners who want to change looks constantly through the year, not just at Christmas. **Verdict: Buy** if reliable Wi-Fi reaches your roofline.

## 2. Trex Lighting (DEKOR): best for homes built around outdoor living spaces

Trex Lighting, sold under the DEKOR platform, ties roofline lighting into the same app that controls deck and hardscape lighting for homes already running Trex decking products. It's built for whole-yard consistency rather than roofline-only control.

**Trex Lighting pros:**
- One app manages deck, path, and roofline zones together
- Low-voltage 12-volt wiring is standard across the ecosystem, simplifying future expansion
- Solid daily-use reliability for basic warm-white and seasonal color switching

**Trex Lighting cons:**
- Fewer dedicated holiday presets compared to Gemstone Lights
- Best value shows up when you already own other Trex outdoor products; standalone roofline buyers get less ecosystem benefit

**Best for:** properties with an existing outdoor living space where lighting needs to match the deck, not just the roofline. **Verdict: Buy** for Trex-ecosystem homes, **Hold** if you have no other Trex products.

## 3. EverLights: best for simple zone control without the learning curve

EverLights strips the app down to fewer menus and fewer decisions, which works for homeowners who want a clean on/off/color schedule and nothing more complicated.

**EverLights pros:**
- Fastest setup of the systems compared here
- Straightforward zone toggles instead of layered scene menus
- Works well for households that mainly want a warm-white default with occasional color for holidays

**EverLights cons:**
- Scene libraries are thinner than Gemstone Lights or Kichler
- Less granular zone splitting on larger, multi-section rooflines

**Best for:** homeowners who tried a competitor's app once, found it confusing, and want something they'll actually use in 2026 and beyond. **Verdict: Buy** for simplicity-first buyers.

## 4. Kichler Permanent Lighting: best for whole-property integration

Kichler brings decades of landscape lighting hardware into its permanent roofline line, and the app reflects that background by treating path lights, uplighting, and roofline LEDs as one connected system rather than separate zones bolted together.

**Kichler pros:**
- Manages roofline and landscape lighting from a single app
- Reliable scheduling for properties with mixed lighting types
- Established hardware track record in the landscape lighting space

**Kichler cons:**
- Menu structure takes longer to master when layering multiple scenes
- Less color-scene depth than Gemstone Lights for pure roofline display use

**Best for:** homeowners upgrading landscape lighting and roofline lighting at the same time. **Verdict: Buy** for full-property projects, **Hold** if you only want roofline coverage.

## 5. Lumilum: best for installer-programmed scenes with minimal homeowner input

Lumilum leans toward professional commissioning over consumer self-service. The installer sets zones, schedules, and holiday transitions at install time, and the homeowner interacts with the system far less than with the other four platforms.

**Lumilum pros:**
- Lower day-to-day complexity since the installer handles programming
- Consistent, professionally tuned scenes from day one
- Good fit for homeowners who don't want to manage an app at all

**Lumilum cons:**
- Changing a scene later usually means calling the installer back, not opening an app
- Fewer self-service options than Gemstone Lights or Kichler

**Best for:** homeowners who want the display handled, not managed. **Verdict: Hold** unless you're comfortable relying on your installer for changes.

## How we ranked

Each system was weighed against the six criteria above: zone granularity, scheduling automation, color/scene depth, smart home integration, connectivity reliability, and installer support model. Gemstone Lights led on scene depth and integration; Trex Lighting and Kichler led on whole-property consistency; EverLights led on simplicity; Lumilum led on hands-off reliability.



## Which permanent lighting system should you choose?

For most homeowners weighing permanent lighting systems app control features in 2026, **Gemstone Lights is the default pick** if your Wi-Fi signal reaches the roofline reliably. Choose **Trex Lighting or Kichler** if you're integrating deck, path, and roofline lighting into one project. Choose **EverLights** if the app itself is the deciding factor and you want the fewest menus. Choose **Lumilum** only if you're fine calling your installer for scene changes rather than doing it yourself.

Any of these systems needs correct roofline mounting to perform well long-term, which is where install quality separates a five-year display from a one-season disappointment. A crew that also evaluates gutter condition during the same visit — checking for sagging fascia or channel damage that could interfere with a mounting run — catches problems before the lighting goes up, not after.

## FAQ


**What are the best permanent lighting systems for app control in 2026?**

Gemstone Lights ranks highest for scene customization and smart home integration in 2026, with Trex Lighting and Kichler close behind for whole-property control. EverLights suits homeowners who want the simplest app experience.

**Is Gemstone Lights better than Trex Lighting?**

Gemstone Lights offers deeper color scene design and voice assistant integration, while Trex Lighting wins for homes that already run Trex decking and want one app for deck, path, and roofline lighting together.

**Do permanent lighting systems need Wi-Fi to work?**

Most consumer app-based systems, including Gemstone Lights and Kichler, need a stable 2.4GHz Wi-Fi connection at the roofline to control scenes and schedules. Systems without a strong signal at that location can drop connectivity intermittently.

**Can I control permanent roofline lighting with Alexa or Google Home?**

Gemstone Lights and several competing platforms integrate with Alexa and Google Home for voice control of on/off and preset scenes. Integration depth varies by brand, so check compatibility before installation.

**How much does permanent lighting installation cost?**

Cost depends on roofline length, number of zones, and system chosen, and varies by property. A detailed cost breakdown is available for homes in South Jersey, Eastern Pennsylvania, and Northern Delaware.

**Do I need a professional installer for a permanent lighting system?**

Professional installation matters for mounting integrity along the roofline, especially on older fascia, and several systems like Lumilum are designed around installer-programmed commissioning rather than homeowner setup.

**What's the difference between permanent lighting and holiday string lights?**

Permanent lighting systems are low-voltage LED channels mounted year-round under the roofline and controlled through an app, unlike temporary holiday string lights that get hung and removed seasonally.

**Can permanent lighting run year-round, not just for holidays?**

Yes, permanent lighting systems are built for 24/7/365 operation, switching between warm-white daily use and color scenes for holidays or events through the app.


## One last thing

The app matters less than the mounting once the first storm hits. A permanent lighting channel installed on a sagging fascia board or over a gutter run that's already failing won't stay level or watertight, no matter how good the scene library looks in the app — get the roofline structure checked before you pick a system, not after.
